scenarios.name: single-dimension fill collapse
scenarios.edge_case: The baseline case: one segment's own rate steps down.

scenarios.name: uniform global request drop
scenarios.edge_case: Every segment moves together — no segment explains >=50%. The agent must NOT force-name a scapegoat segment.

scenarios.name: mix shift, no rate change
scenarios.edge_case: Traffic reshuffles toward a naturally weaker ad_format. Global fill falls while EVERY segment's own fill is flat. A naive sweep reads 'uniform' and would say GLOBAL; the Kitagawa split must catch that the mix term dominates.

scenarios.name: interaction segment (os_version x region)
scenarios.edge_case: Cause is the CROSS of two dimensions, not either alone. Single-dim sweeps see a partial signal on both and confounder-elimination shrinks but never clears the residual.

scenarios.name: advertiser demand pullout
scenarios.edge_case: A vertical stops bidding. fill_rate BY vertical is undefined (unfilled rows carry no advertiser), so the ratio sweep is structurally blind — only a volume sweep on fills finds it.

scenarios.name: CTR spike (click fraud), revenue flat
scenarios.edge_case: An UP move, not a drop — thresholds must be abs(). Revenue stays flat, so it is not a monetisation win; the narrative must not read it as good news.

scenarios.name: partial-day onset (08:00-17:00 only)
scenarios.edge_case: Measured across the whole calendar day the move dilutes below threshold; the window must follow detection's hour buckets, not the date.

scenarios.name: unseen dimension values (dictionary miss)
scenarios.edge_case: New geo_device_ids absent from the dim table. dictGetOrDefault sends them to the 'unknown' bucket; an inner join would silently DROP the very rows that moved. Closest analogue to release-day data carrying values we have never seen.

scenarios.name: two independent simultaneous incidents
scenarios.edge_case: Two unrelated levers move on the same day (a fill collapse and an eCPM drop). Diagnosing one must not close the other.

scenarios.name: ingestion gap (zero events 02:00-06:00)
scenarios.edge_case: Absence of data is itself a finding. A volume 'drop' that is really a pipeline hole must not be attributed to a segment.

scenarios.name: eCPM price drop on one campaign_type
scenarios.edge_case: Price lever rather than volume/fill — exercises the eCPM branch and its advertiser-side dimensions.

scenarios.name: slow ramp, day 1 of 3 (-5%)
scenarios.edge_case: A drift, not a step. Each day alone may sit under threshold and the ramp poisons its own trailing baseline; step detection can miss it.
scenarios.note: Day 1 legitimately may not flag — see EDGE_CASES.md

scenarios.name: slow ramp, day 2 of 3 (-10%)
scenarios.edge_case: Mid-ramp. Still no step change on any single day.

scenarios.name: slow ramp, day 3 of 3 (-15%)
scenarios.edge_case: By day 3 cumulative drift should clear threshold even though no single day is a step.

scenarios.name: SEASONALITY: real collapse on the lowest-traffic day (Sunday)
scenarios.edge_case: The masking test. Sunday already runs -19% on volume, so a flat or pooled baseline attributes the drop to the weekend and dismisses a genuine incident. Only a same-weekday baseline (Sunday vs prior Sundays) still sees it. This is the false-NEGATIVE that seasonality causes.

scenarios.name: SEASONALITY: weekend-sized volume drop on a WEEKDAY
scenarios.edge_case: The mirror test. -19% is normal on Sunday and an incident on Wednesday — the SAME number. A baseline that is not weekday-aware must fail exactly one of S15/S16, so passing both is the real proof the seasonality handling works.

scenarios.name: peer outlier on a history-free slice
scenarios.edge_case: Too few days for any same-weekday baseline. q1/q2/q3/q5 are all impossible; only sibling comparison inside the window can find the outlier. This is the release-day shape if the unseen slice ships without history.
